newsitem.title: LATVIA: NEXT TWO-YEAR T-BILL AUCTION IN SIX MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: NEXT TWO-YEAR T-BILL AUCTION IN SIX MONTHS.

text.p: Latvia's state exchequer said on Thursday that the country's next auction for two-year Treasury bills will be held in six months' time.
"The next two-year government T-bill auction will be held in six months' time," Aivars Veiss, head of the state exchequer, told a news conference.
"The introduction of the two-year maturity will reduce the amount of short-term T-bills being offered," Veiss said.
Latvia held its first two-year T-bill auction on Wednesday and the response was very positive, especially from foreign investors.
The 17 million lat issue fetched over 48 million lats worth of bids and the average yield was 9.52 percent.
Veiss said that one-month and three-month paper will continue to be auctioned every week while six-month bills will now be sold every two weeks.
One-year government debt paper will be sold once every six weeks, he said.
